speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: asked the Minister for Education whether Autonomous Universities can provide clear communications with their students whenever there are allegations of misconduct involving teaching staff and students so that students can be better protected.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: If the case involves a student or staff from the same institution, the IHLs may also impose a No-Contact Order to ensure that the alleged offender is prohibited from contacting or being in the vicinity of the party making the allegations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: A Police report is typically made for allegations of serious misconduct, and where the alleged offender is proven and charged in Court, this will be a matter of public record.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Separately, the IHLs also conduct their own internal investigations to determine if the alleged offender has breached their Code of Conduct.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Those who do so are subject to disciplinary sanctions, including possible suspension or expulsion of students, or dismissal of staff.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: In the course of addressing allegations, MOE expects institutions to be open and timely in their communications, while taking into consideration the facts of the case, the need to ensure the safety of their communities and safeguard the well-being and privacy of victims and other members of the community who are directly impacted, and the need to ensure that Police investigations are not impacted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: MOE will continue to work closely with the IHLs to ensure that the well-being and safety of students and staff on campus are protected.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, may I ask the Minister of State, what is the time frame when we say that MOE expects the institution to be open and timely in their communications with the students.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: As an undergraduate, if you are approaching a lecturer, you would want to know whether the lecturer is under investigation and whether the lecturer is likely to be a predator.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Given the unequal relationship between a student and a lecturer, I think it is justifiable that a student would ask for timely disclosure, so that they would be able to know and assess how to deal with the lecturer.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In that sense, may I ask MOE how would the Ministry want to keep the student community safe in circumstances like that?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Can I also ask MOE whether they can provide this House with an update on the number of similar incidents in the past years?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We agree that communication is very important and we will ask the IHLs to do more on this front, while bearing in mind the context and specificities of each case.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In the present case regarding this specific lecturer, I have shared that NUS required the accused individual to stay away from campus and that a No-Contact Order was swiftly made out.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These were carried out and disclosed by NUS in its media conference.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We do not condone instances of sexual misconduct as well as sexual offences that happen on campus.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MOE will work closely with the IHLs to protect our students.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This translates to an incidence rate of around 0.21 sexual misconduct cases involving student perpetrators per 1,000 students.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In 2018, the AUs handled 17 such cases.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In 2019, the number of such cases fell to 14 with a corresponding incidence rate of 0.13.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If we look at the IHLs as a total and if we look at sexual misconduct cases committed by both students and staff, the IHLs handled a total of 172 disciplinary cases involving sexual misconduct committed by students and staff from 2015 to 2019.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This translates to an incidence rate of 0.12 sexual misconduct cases involving staff and student perpetrators per 1,000 staff and students.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I also want to add that our IHLs are key public institutions and they are expected to uphold high academic standards and professionalism.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They also owe a duty of care to their students.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That is why we have zero tolerance when it comes to sexual misconduct instances that happen on campus.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There can be open discussions; we have very bright teaching faculty, we have students who are also discovering themselves, exploring their passions.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But all that said, these discussions must have academic rigour and be constructive.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Staff are expected to uphold professional codes of conduct in their interactions with students.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: When there is a breach of the IHLs' codes of conduct, the punishments are swift.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Students can be suspended, they can be dismissed from school and the same goes for staff.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And we see that in this case, the teaching staff was dismissed very quickly and NUS has shared that it will endeavour to do better when it comes to communications.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There is some overlap in the two questions.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, if I may just take the two of them together.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, I hope that helps to allay the concerns that the Member has.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Member has asked about what happens in Secondary schools at the younger ages and at tertiary education, I think we all recognise that different age groups have a different understanding of sexuality.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have to ensure that sexuality education is targeted in its delivery.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, starting from Primary schools, students are made aware of how they can protect themselves.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In Secondary schools, teachers also provide certain scenarios so that students are aware of how they can protect themselves.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Specialised training for sexuality education teachers is conducted by very specialised staff within MOE.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In sum, MOE takes this very seriously how students of different ages can protect themselves, and we deliver that education in a targeted manner.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Where, unfortunately, a sexual offence has occurred and victims require help and support, we have dedicated personnel, who serve as the first line of support for the victims.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They centralise the care and support, and students and affected individuals do not have to go about looking for different individuals for help.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They can go directly to the dedicated personnel.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The first is whether there are any plans to make any investigations into such complaints about sexual violence and sexual misconduct, whether to make them independent to give students better confidence?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, basically, independent in the sense that it is not undertaken by the Universities or the institutions themselves.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: My second question is, as Ms Carrie Tan mentioned earlier, the Minister of State has responded regarding Secondary school level, steps taken for these students to make sure that they are aware of sexuality and issues relating to consent, is the Ministry taking any proactive steps to making sure to examine whether this is also a problem at younger levels, and whether there is any studies being conducted at the Secondary school level to see whether there are any problems?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, just being proactive and find out whether it is an issue.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There is a certain structure in the Board of Discipline; students are also included in the Board of Discipline to provide their perspectives on the issue.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Investigations are carried out through campus security and the issue is very seriously considered by the senior management of the IHLs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Separate from that, there is the criminal justice system.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That is with regard to the first question that the Member highlighted.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On the second question with regard to Secondary school students, we take in feedback from parents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Sexuality education is such that it does not happen in a vacuum.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I mentioned earlier about scenarios being used to teach students; or, rather, to also solicit inputs from them.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Otherwise, as part of the education process, we do not really quite know whether the students have imbibed what has been taught.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, sexuality education educators are well aware of the sensitivities around this topic and when they teach it in classrooms, they are very sensitive about it and then use scenarios, so that the students best know how to apply those lessons to undertake self-care.
